title: zebRabox: an R package for ZebraBox data treatment
text: From raw data to interactive visualization.

title: zebRabox: an R package for ZebraBox data treatment
text:
Introduction
The ZebraBox chamber is a complete system for high-throughput behavioral tests. Applications include pharmacology, toxicology, ecotoxicology, and behavioral genetics. The device holds 6-, 12-, 24-, 48- or 96-well plates and has a high-resolution camera which films in visible or infrared light. Tests run from minutes to days and each data point links to a fixed time window (integration period). Output files are .raw and .xls.

title: zebRabox: an R package for ZebraBox data treatment
text:
Why zebRabox?
Data in many files and formats leads to errors, duplicates, and manual fixes. zebRabox is an R package that wraps a Shiny application to centralize everything in one place. You get accurate, up-to-date, and auditable results without writing code. 

Simple : drag, drop, clean, merge, and analyze in a few clicks.

title: zebRabox: an R package for ZebraBox data treatment
text:
How to Use zebRabox?

Install the package
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Antoine-T17/zebRabox", dependencies = TRUE, upgrade = "never")


Launch the app
zebRabox::run_app()


Load or Create a Plate Plan
ZebraBox uses standard multi-well plates. Edge wells can show border effects. The app can generate a random plan. Download it as .xlsx or view it as a table and figure. If you already have a plan, load it and wait to see Upload complete to click on the button. Column names must follow the required format. What is the required format? Download a 96-well sample plate plan.


Load Raw Data
Raw files must be in .xlsx. Convert your original .xls files before loading. When loading, wait to see Upload complete to click on the button.

The number of raw files must match your plate plans.



Choose Primary Mode

Tracking mode
Follows each subject’s path.
Yields distance moved, active time, and movement counts.
Refer to the guidelines provided by the supplier for details.
Quantization mode
Counts pixel color changes.
Yields high, medium, or low activity levels.
Refer to the guidelines provided by the supplier for details.



Choose Secondary Mode

Light/Dark (LDM)
For experiments with light shifts (0–100% or 100–0%).
Works even if no change occurred.
Vibration/Rest (VM)
For experiments with vibration frequencies (Hz).

title: zebRabox: an R package for ZebraBox data treatment
text:
Processing Data

Match Raw Data to Plate Plans
Confirm that each raw data file is correctly paired with its corresponding plate plan. Use the dropdown menu to select the appropriate plate plan.


Additional Parameters
Before running full processing, upload your period transition file and removal specification file. Both must be .xlsx files with column names in the required format. What is the required format? Download a sample period transition file and a sample removal specification file.


Run Full Processing
After you start processing, follow each step in the Console Output. When it finishes, explore results in the Processed Data tab or download them for external analysis.

title: zebRabox: an R package for ZebraBox data treatment
text:
Visualize Data
Choose a plot type and generate the dataset. Check the Console Output to confirm the generation completed successfully. The Visualization tab is designed for quick data exploration. For deeper customization, download the processed data or the generated plot datasets.
You can configure and export figures with:

Theme: light or dark

Zone selection: restrict to specific zones (if applicable)

X-axis label order: define a custom order

Label color: set category/condition colors

Save options: export each figure as PNG


Boxplots
Visualize distributions across transition periods (e.g., Light/Dark or Vibration/Rest).


Cumulative Boxplots
View overall distributions independent of transition periods.


Delta Boxplots
Compare values before, during, and after a selected transition period to pinpoint responses (e.g., escape/avoidance) to stimuli.


Line Plots
Track activity or movement patterns over time to reveal trends and temporal dynamics.

title: Antoine Tourret - Curriculum Vitae
text:
Professional Summary
PhD candidate in aquatic ecotoxicology at the Laboratoire Eau Environnement et Systèmes Urbains (LEESU, Université Paris-Est Créteil). My research focuses on the effects of micro- and nanoplastics and their associated additives on the freshwater crustacean Daphnia magna. I combine standardised and sub-acute bioassays, behavioural endpoints and the chemical characterisation (target and non-target screening) of plastic leachates. I previously worked on optical brighteners, glyphosate and AMPA, using microalgae, freshwater biofilms and zebrafish larvae. I teach biostatistics and ecotoxicology (about 125 hours since 2024), supervise interns and analyse my data in R, with a particular taste for data visualisation and reproducible reporting with Quarto. I am currently training in regulatory ecotoxicology (REACH, CLP, environmental risk assessment).

title: Antoine Tourret
text:
I am a PhD student at Université Paris-Est Créteil, within the Laboratoire Eau Environnements et Systèmes Urbains (LEESU).
My research is focused on aquatic ecotoxicology, and I’m using Daphnia magna as a biological model.

title: Antoine Tourret
text:
Research
I am currently working on a project that aims to assess the ecotoxicity of model nanoplastics synthesised by the Institut des Sciences Analytiques et de Physico-Chimie pour l’Environnement et les Matériaux (IPREM, Pau). The project has two complementary components: on the one hand, the toxicity of pristine nanoplastics, and on the other, the toxicity of the same nanoplastics after several hours of photodegradation. Using identical samples allows a direct comparison between non-degraded and degraded nanoplastics.
I am also working on another project that aims to evaluate the ecotoxicity of urban furniture made from recycled plastic. To do so, leaching experiments will be conducted, combined with chemical and ecotoxicological screening.

title: Antoine Tourret
text:
Beyond the lab
I have a passion for clouds. Identifying their forms, watching them evolve and transform within minutes, capturing them at just the right moment before they vanish.
Find my photos on Instagram: @antoine_cumulus.
I also enjoy everything related to data visualization, building clear, elegant, and reproducible reports with Quarto.
One last thing: I own more than thirty ties and wear them pratically everyday (except when the weather is too hot).

title: Antoine Tourret - Curriculum Vitae
text:
Regulatory Ecotoxicology

Standardised test guidelines (hands-on): OECD 201 (algal growth inhibition), OECD 202 (Daphnia acute immobilisation) and OECD 236 (fish embryo acute toxicity), with derivation of ECx values by dose–response modelling in R.
Self-training in progress (since November 2026), based on professional training material in regulatory ecotoxicology:

EU REACH Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006: registration process, roles in the supply chain, standard information requirements according to tonnage (Annexes VII to X), IUCLID 6 dossier preparation and REACH-IT submission.
CLP Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 and UN GHS: hazard classification of substances and mixtures, including acute and chronic aquatic hazards.
Environmental risk assessment: PEC/PNEC approach, PNEC derivation with assessment factors, exposure scenarios with Chesar.
PBT/vPvB assessment, environmental fate (biodegradation, bioaccumulation) and in silico approaches (QSAR, read-across, OECD QSAR Toolbox).

Academic background: regulatory modules of the Master’s in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Chemistry (University of Bordeaux).
